What the official sources say

  • New Castle County: written notice of assessment appeal must be filed with the Board of Assessment Review before March 15; Board gives at least 10 days' notice of hearing; failure to appear is abandonment. (9 Del. C. ch. 83, subch. I (Board of Assessment Review); source)
  • If an appeal reduces assessed value and the owner overpaid by $50 or more, the owner is entitled to a refund; under $50 the county may refund or credit it. (9 Del. C. ch. 83, subch. I; source)
  • The board must notify the appellant of its decision in writing by registered mail within 30 days of the decision. (9 Del. C. ch. 83, subch. I; source)
  • An aggrieved appellant may appeal to Superior Court within 30 days (postmark) after receiving notice of the decision; the board's decision is prima facie correct and the appellant must show it acted contrary to law, fraudulently, arbitrarily or capriciously. (9 Del. C. ch. 83, subch. I; source)
  • The court will not approve a sale if the owner is ready at court to pay taxes, penalty and costs. (9 Del. C. ch. 87, subch. IV; source)
Selling in Delaware?
We buy Delaware houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Who bills property tax in Delaware?

Delaware property tax is billed locally, by county tax offices, and the rate you pay depends mostly on your school district. Kent County's assessment office says the tax is the taxable value multiplied by the rate, with the school district setting most of that rate and the county government and county library adding to it.

That means two houses with the same value can get different bills, even inside one county. A home in the Colonial school district in New Castle County is billed on different rates than one in Appoquinimink. When you plan a sale, read the bill for your own parcel and the district printed on it, not a neighbor's number.

Delaware has only three counties, so the structure is simple to keep in your head.

  • New Castle County: the northern county, with five school districts that lie entirely within it plus a vocational-technical district.
  • Kent County: the middle county, billed by the Kent County Receiver of Taxes.
  • Sussex County: the southern county, billed through the Sussex County Treasury and Billing offices in Georgetown.

Why did Delaware reassess every property recently?

Delaware reassessed because a court ordered it after decades without new values. Spotlight Delaware reports that New Castle and Kent counties had not reassessed since the 1980s and Sussex had not done so since 1974, and that a 2020 Court of Chancery ruling followed a 2018 lawsuit over the old system.

The same reporting says House Bill 62 now requires each county to reassess every five years. Kent County's current values are as of July 1, 2023, according to the county's assessment FAQ. New Castle County's values are as of July 1, 2024.

For a seller, the reassessment matters in two ways. First, your assessed value now tracks market value much more closely than it did, so a buyer or a cash investor reading your bill will see a number tied to a recent date. Second, Spotlight Delaware notes that roughly a third of owners saw lower taxes, a third higher and a third about the same, and that exemptions and abatements were not built into the new assessed values. They are applied once a rate is set.

Kent County's FAQ adds that a sale does not trigger a reassessment.

When are Delaware property taxes due?

In Kent and Sussex counties the annual bill is due September 30. New Castle County's tax code sets a July 1 due date with a penalty that starts after September 1, so New Castle owners should read their own bill for the exact deadline.

CountyTax yearBills mailedDueLate cost
KentJune 1 to May 31Typically by mid-August, after school districts set ratesSeptember 30Ask the Kent Tax Office
SussexJuly 1 to June 30Early AugustSeptember 30 (supplemental bills Dec. 31, Mar. 31, June 30)1.5% per month
New CastleSet by 9 Del. C. ch. 86Statement within 30 days after the due dateJuly 1 under 9 Del. C. 86016% after September 1, then 1% each month

Sussex County adds that a missing bill does not cancel a penalty. Its tax office says the owner is responsible for paying on time even if the bill never arrived. New Castle's code says the same thing: not receiving a statement does not excuse timely payment.

New Castle's code also requires the Office of Finance to send at least one written demand for unpaid taxes by December 15 each year. A residential owner with a primary residence and a bill at least $300 above the prior year can qualify for a payment plan of at least three equal school-tax installments. Those plan provisions are written to expire on August 12, 2028.

What are the school tax rates in New Castle County?

New Castle County school districts split their rates in 2025, charging homes a lower rate than apartments, commercial and industrial property. Spotlight Delaware published the new per-$100 rates after the school boards voted in August 2025.

DistrictResidential rateNon-residential rate
Appoquinimink0.576921.15378
Brandywine0.56091.0382
Christina0.61501.2102
Colonial0.45230.74294
Red Clay0.59180.99237
NCC Vo-Tech0.03760.0608

To estimate a school bill, divide the assessment by 100 and multiply by the residential rate for the district. The same source says the county aimed to mail recalculated bills by September 30, 2025, with a November 30 payment date, and that overpayments of more than $50 could be refunded or credited.

Rates change every year, so treat this as a snapshot of how the split works rather than a quote for the current bill.

Which exemptions and credits can lower a Delaware tax bill?

Delaware offers a school tax credit for seniors, a county exemption for low-income seniors and the disabled, and full exemptions for government, school, religious and some charitable property. Most of them require an application, and most have a spring deadline.

  • Senior School Property Tax Credit: the state Department of Finance says the owner must be 65 or older and the property must be the primary residence. Applications are due April 30. Residency rules depend on when you became a Delaware domiciliary: before 2013, no waiting period beyond eligibility in the following tax year; from 2013 through 2017, three consecutive years; from January 1, 2018, ten consecutive years. The bill must be paid in full by the end of the tax year. The state's page shows two different maximum amounts, so confirm the current cap with your county before you rely on a figure.
  • Kent County senior and disability exemption: age 65 by May 31 or total disability, income limits of $18,000 for one applicant or $24,750 combined with a spouse, and yearly reapplication by April 30. Title must be in the applicant's name.
  • General exemptions: government property, school property used for education, religious property not held as an investment, certain charitable property and parkland owned by civic groups such as homeowners' associations.

Sussex County sends applications for its senior, disability and State 65 exemptions through the Billing Office at (302) 855-7871.

How do I appeal a Delaware property assessment?

You appeal in writing to your county, and deadlines are firm. In Kent County an annual appeal must reach the Assessment Office by 5:00 p.m. on January 31 to affect the tax year beginning June 1, and a postmark is not accepted. Appeals of quarterly supplemental increases must be filed within 30 days of notice. The county notes that deadlines can change in reassessment years.

During the reassessment, Spotlight Delaware described a two-step path: an informal review with the contractor, Tyler Technologies, and then an appeal through the county. For New Castle County, the official summary at the top of this page gives the Board of Assessment Review deadline of March 15.

The refund rules deserve attention before a sale. Kent County says its refund policy follows state law and covers limited cases, such as tax paid while an appeal is pending or a duplicate bill. An error found after the appeal window usually does not produce a refund. Delaware law, in the county's words, puts the burden of making sure assessment data is accurate on the property owner.

If you plan to sell, an appeal that is still open at closing is a loose end. Tell the title company about it so the proceeds and any refund are handled in writing.

What happens if I sell a Delaware house with property tax due?

Unpaid property tax in Delaware is collected out of the sale or, if it goes unpaid long enough, through a court-supervised tax sale. The seller should expect the title company to find the balance and pay it from proceeds at closing.

Under the monition method in the Delaware Code, the tax collector files in Superior Court, the sheriff posts a notice on the property, and the notice gives 20 days to pay before the tax authority can ask for a sale. After a tax sale the owner has 60 days after court approval to redeem by paying the purchaser the price plus 15 percent and costs. Kent County's sheriff procedures also describe tax sales held about every three months, with the full bid due the same day.

Practical steps for an owner with a bill outstanding:

  • Pull the current bill and any supplemental bills from the county tax portal.
  • Check whether a mortgage escrow already paid it. Sussex County offers an EscrowCheck tool and forwards bills to mortgage companies.
  • After closing, report the ownership change to the county assessment office. Sussex lists (302) 855-7824 for ownership changes.
  • Keep proof of payment for any exemption you are leaving behind.

A cash buyer who purchases a house as-is can close with the tax balance paid from proceeds, which is often the simplest route when back taxes are growing by the month. Cash Home Buyers can talk through your balance, but any figure depends on the county records for your parcel.

More questions about Delaware Property Tax Guide

Does Delaware have a state property tax?

The sources used for this guide describe property tax as billed by counties and school districts, and none of them describes a state-level levy. Your bill comes from the county tax office and reflects your school district's rate.

When is the Delaware property tax due date?

Kent and Sussex counties list September 30 for the annual bill. New Castle County's code sets July 1 with penalties after September 1, so check the due date printed on your New Castle bill.

Will selling my house trigger a new assessment?

Not in Kent County. Its assessment office says a sale does not trigger reassessment, and values change only for a countywide reassessment, a change to the property or a corrected error. Delaware counties now reassess every five years.

Can seniors reduce Delaware property tax?

Yes. The state Senior School Property Tax Credit covers homeowners 65 and older on their primary residence, with an April 30 application deadline. Kent County also has an income-limited senior and disability exemption. Confirm the current credit amount with your county.

What happens if I do not pay my Delaware property tax?

Penalties start, such as 1.5% per month in Sussex County and 6% after September 1 plus 1% a month in New Castle County. Continued non-payment can lead to a monition tax sale, where the owner has 60 days after court approval to redeem by paying the buyer the price plus 15 percent.

Can I sell a Delaware house to a cash buyer if I owe back taxes?

Yes, in many cases. The tax balance is paid from the sale proceeds at closing, and the title company confirms the payoff with the county. The earlier you sell, the less penalty builds up.

title: Delaware Estate and Inheritance Tax: What Heirs Owe When Selling
content:
Delaware Estate and Inheritance Tax: What Heirs Owe When Selling

Cash Home Buyers in Delaware
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Delaware Estate and Inheritance Tax: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Delaware Estate and Inheritance Tax sale
  • Turn the Delaware Estate and Inheritance Tax offer down and you owe us nothing

Selling a Delaware House? Get a Cash Offer

We buy as-is.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

What the official sources say

  • Delaware imposed an estate tax only on individuals dying before January 1, 2018; the estate tax was repealed for individuals dying after Dec 31, 2017. (Estate Tax | Delaware Division of Revenue; source)
Selling in Delaware?
We buy Delaware houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Does Delaware have an estate tax or inheritance tax today?

No. Delaware has neither tax for people who die after December 31, 2017. The Division of Revenue's estate tax summary records that the estate tax was repealed for individuals dying after that date, under 81 Del. Laws c. 52 (HB 16).

The inheritance tax went first. Chapter 13 of Title 30 of the Delaware Code, the inheritance tax chapter, now carries the label "Repealed." The Division's legislative history says a 1998 law repealed the inheritance tax effective January 1, 1999 and revised the estate tax to apply to estates large enough to need a federal estate tax return.

For heirs who plan to sell a Delaware house, that is good news about one cost and no news about the others. The state does not tax the inheritance itself, but the sale can still trigger realty transfer tax, county property tax and possibly federal rules.

How did Delaware's estate tax work before the repeal?

For deaths before January 1, 2018, Delaware taxed the value of an estate at death, using the federal estate tax as its starting point. It is worth knowing if the person who owned your house died in 2017 or earlier.

The Division of Revenue explains that a resident's Delaware taxable estate was the modified federal taxable estate, reduced but not below zero by the federal applicable exclusion amount. For 2017 that exclusion was $5,490,000 for an individual. The Division's rate table was graduated, and Morris Nichols reports a top rate capped at 16%.

DateChange
July 1, 1998 (effective January 1, 1999)Inheritance tax repealed; estate tax revised to follow the federal return requirement
July 1, 2009Estate tax effectively reinstated with a four-year sunset
March 28, 2013Sunset eliminated
July 2, 2017 (effective January 1, 2018)Estate tax repealed for individuals dying after December 31, 2017

Source: Delaware Division of Revenue, Estate Tax summary, legislative history.

What if the owner died before 2018 and the estate is still open?

Then the old rules may still matter, and you should ask the Register of Wills or an estate attorney. The repealed sections of Chapter 15 of Title 30 carry notes pointing to 81 Del. Laws c. 52, section 2 about how the repeal applies.

The Division's filing rules for the old tax were these:

  • The return and the tax were due within nine months after the date of death.
  • The Division could extend filing and payment time on written request. If the federal return was extended, the Delaware return was extended for a like period.
  • Interest ran at one-half of one percent per month on late tax, and penalties could include a failure-to-pay penalty of 1% per month up to 25%.
  • For nonresidents, a special lien attached to Delaware real and tangible property until the tax was paid.

The Sussex County Register of Wills publishes form NDETRR99, an affidavit that no Delaware estate tax return is required, for decedents who died from January 1, 1999 through December 31, 2017. It is signed before a notary by the personal representative or a surviving joint tenant, lists any Delaware real property, and cites 30 Del. C. 1505. An older estate that never cleared title may need that paper before a buyer will close.

Could federal estate tax still apply to a Delaware house?

Federal estate tax applies only to very large estates. The IRS says the basic exclusion amount is $15,000,000 for calendar year 2026, up from $13,990,000 for 2025.

The IRS also says a surviving spouse can elect to take over the decedent's unused exclusion on a timely filed estate tax return. That election has been available since January 1, 2011.

The statewide median home value is far below the exclusion, so a federal return is rarely the issue for one house. We are not tax preparers. If the estate holds many assets or you are unsure, ask a CPA or estate attorney.

Do heirs owe realty transfer tax when a Delaware house changes hands?

Sometimes. Delaware's realty transfer tax is a separate tax from the estate tax, and some transfers within families are excluded from it. The rules are in Chapter 54 of Title 30.

Section 5401(1) says a taxable "document" does not include a will or a transfer on death deed. It also excludes conveyances between spouses, between parent and child or the child's spouse, between siblings, half siblings or step siblings, and between grandparent and grandchild or the grandchild's spouse.

A sale to an outside buyer is a different matter. Under section 5402, the rate is 3% of value unless the county or municipality has enacted the full 1.5% local tax, in which case it is 2.5%. The Division's instructions put the combined state and local total at 4%, with 2.5% to the state and 1.5% to the county or municipality. The tax is apportioned equally between grantor and grantee, and under section 5412, absent a contrary agreement, the burden of paying falls on the grantor.

The instructions list estates and trusts among grantor categories but, in the text we reviewed, do not describe a special estate exemption. If a personal representative is signing the deed, confirm the treatment with the county Recorder of Deeds.

What does selling an inherited Delaware house usually involve?

The steps run through probate, title and the county. Delaware's three counties, New Castle, Kent and Sussex, each have their own Register of Wills and Recorder of Deeds, so the office depends on where the house sits.

  • Open the estate with the Register of Wills in the county, and have the personal representative appointed.
  • Resolve any open estate tax paperwork if the death was before 2018.
  • Pay or settle county and school property taxes. Under Title 9, taxes in New Castle and Sussex are due July 1 and in Kent June 1.
  • Sign a deed and pay realty transfer tax at recording, with proof of payment on the document. A deed without it cannot be recorded under section 5408.
  • Deliver the house in the condition the contract requires. A cash sale can be as-is.

Late county taxes cost money. In New Castle County the collecting authority adds a 6% penalty after September 1 plus 1% a month on the unpaid balance. In Kent and Sussex a penalty of 1.5% per month starts after September 30 of the year the tax duplicate is delivered.

What do Delaware housing numbers look like for heirs?

Delaware is mostly owner-occupied, and nearly a quarter of residents are 65 or older. The Census Bureau supplies the basics.

MeasureDelaware
Population estimate, July 1, 20251,059,952
Persons 65 and over22.8%
Housing units, July 1, 2025483,447
Owner-occupied housing unit rate, 2020 to 202473.0%
Median value of owner-occupied units, 2020 to 2024$352,000

Source: U.S. Census Bureau QuickFacts. The median value is a statewide figure for owner-occupied homes, not an appraisal of any one house.

If you inherited a Delaware house you do not want to keep, a cash buyer can close as-is, which spares repairs and clean-out on a property in a distant county. Terms vary by house, and we recommend you have an attorney review the estate side.

More questions about Delaware Estate and Inheritance Tax

Is there a Delaware inheritance tax?

No. Chapter 13 of Title 30, the inheritance tax chapter, is marked repealed, and the Division of Revenue records the inheritance tax repeal as effective January 1, 1999.

When was the Delaware estate tax repealed?

It was repealed for individuals dying after December 31, 2017. The repeal was approved July 2, 2017 as 81 Del. Laws c. 52 (HB 16).

What is the federal estate tax exclusion for 2026?

The IRS lists $15,000,000 as the basic exclusion amount for calendar year 2026, compared with $13,990,000 for 2025.

Do I pay realty transfer tax if I inherit a Delaware house?

A will and a transfer on death deed are not taxable documents, and conveyances between parent and child, siblings, and grandparent and grandchild are also excluded under 30 Del. C. 5401. A sale to an outside buyer is taxed at a combined 4%, split equally between buyer and seller unless the contract says otherwise.

Where do I record the deed for an inherited Delaware house?

Record it with the Recorder of Deeds in the county where the property is located. Proof of realty transfer tax payment, or an affidavit explaining why none is owed, must accompany the document.

title: Delaware Sheriff Sales: Foreclosure Sale Steps and Redemption
content:
Delaware Sheriff Sales: Foreclosure Sale Steps and Redemption

Cash Home Buyers in Delaware
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Delaware Sheriff Sales: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Delaware Sheriff Sales sale
  • Turn the Delaware Sheriff Sales offer down and you owe us nothing

Selling a Delaware House? Get a Cash Offer

We buy as-is.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

What the official sources say

  • A purchaser at a sheriff's sale under a mortgage scire facias holds the property free of the mortgagor's equity of redemption and incumbrances. (10 Del. C. § 5066; source)
  • No judgment may be entered, and no covered owner-occupied 1-4 family residence sold at sheriff's sale, unless the plaintiff has filed the loss-mitigation affidavit. (10 Del. C. § 5062A(b); source)
  • Seller disclosure law does not apply to transfers by sheriff's sale for default on a mortgage, judgment, tax or other lien. (6 Del. C. § 2577(4); source)
  • For owner-occupied 1-4 family primary residences, a foreclosure action may not be filed until 45 days after a notice of intent to foreclose is sent by certified and first-class mail. (10 Del. C. § 5062B(a); source)
  • Plaintiff must file a loss-mitigation affidavit before judgment or sheriff's sale on owner-occupied 1-4 family primary residences. (10 Del. C. § 5062A; source)
  • An Automatic Residential Mortgage Foreclosure Mediation Program applies to owner-occupied 1-4 family primary residences; a mediation notice accompanies the complaint. (10 Del. C. § 5062C; source)
  • A buyer at the foreclosure sale holds the property discharged from all equity of redemption and incumbrances made by the mortgagor. (10 Del. C. § 5066; source)
Selling in Delaware?
We buy Delaware houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

How does a Delaware sheriff sale work?

A Delaware sheriff sale is a public auction of real estate run by the county sheriff to satisfy a court judgment, usually a mortgage foreclosure or unpaid taxes. The sheriff sells to the highest bidder, and the Superior Court then confirms the sale before a deed is delivered.

Delaware has three counties, and each sheriff runs sales a little differently. The sale types you will see are mortgage foreclosure sales, tax sales (also called monition sales) and, in some counties, goods and chattels sales that involve personal property.

  • Foreclosure sales: the plaintiff's attorney gives the opening bid, then bidders raise it verbally.
  • Tax or monition sales: the county or town sells a property for unpaid taxes or fees, and the owner may redeem afterward.
  • Confirmation: the court reviews the sale before the sheriff signs a deed.

For an owner facing a sale date, the practical question is how much time is left and what the options are before the auction.

When and where are sheriff sales held in each county?

Kent County holds mortgage foreclosure sales usually on the first Thursday of the month, and Sussex County holds sales on the third Tuesday of each month at 9:30 a.m. The sales are held at government buildings, not at the property.

ItemKent CountySussex County
Foreclosure sale dayUsually the first Thursday of the month, unless a holidayThird Tuesday of each month, 9:30 a.m.
LocationLevy Court Chambers, 555 Bay Rd., DoverSheriff's Office conference room, 2nd floor, 22215 N. Dupont Blvd., Georgetown
Registration8:30 to 9:30 a.m.9:00 to 9:30 a.m.
Bidder deposit$4,000 per property$4,000 to register
Mortgage sale down payment20% of bid20% of bid
Tax sale paymentFull bid by 2:00 p.m. on sale dayFull bid by 3 p.m. on sale day

Kent County advertises sales in the Dover Post and the Delaware State News two weeks ahead, and tax sales are held about every three months. For New Castle County, the pages we reviewed did not give a current schedule, so check with the New Castle County Sheriff's Office.

What notice must an owner receive before a Delaware sheriff sale?

The sheriff must advertise the sale, and the plaintiff must send notice to interested parties. Under 10 Del. C. section 4973, notice of a real estate sale must be posted at least 10 days before the sale in 10 public places in the county, including the hundred where the property lies and each adjoining hundred, and advertised for two weeks in two newspapers.

Superior Court Civil Rule 69(g) adds a separate mailing duty. At least seven days before the sale, the plaintiff or its counsel must send notice by certified mail, return receipt requested, to lienholders, tenants, record owners and other holders of recorded interests. The notice must also be posted on a common entrance or area of the building. The rule says no sheriff's sale shall be held unless proof of mailing and posting has been filed.

A July 2026 Superior Court order shows why notice matters. In New Castle County v. Coleman, the court set aside a June 9, 2026 sale of a Newark property and denied confirmation because the first mortgage holder never received actual notice that a stay had been lifted. The court noted that the sale price was roughly half of that holder's security interest.

What are the payment and default rules for a successful bidder?

The winning bidder pays a deposit on the day of sale and the balance about a month later. If the bidder fails to pay, the deposit is forfeited and the property is resold.

  • Deposit: $4,000 in Kent County, by cashier's check, certified check or money order payable to the sheriff, applied toward the 20 percent down payment.
  • Foreclosure down payment: Kent requires the rest of the 20 percent by 2:00 p.m. on sale day, with the 80 percent balance due about 30 days later on the third Monday of the following month. Sussex requires 20 percent by 3 p.m. and the balance on the third Monday of the following month.
  • Forfeiture: Kent says a buyer who misses the 2:00 p.m. payment loses the deposit and may be barred from future sales. Sussex says failure to pay the balance forfeits the sale and the non-refundable 20 percent.
  • As-is: Sussex says properties sell as-is and sight unseen, that bidders may not trespass, and that the winner is responsible for any liens.

Neither county guarantees clear title. Both tell bidders to research the Recorder of Deeds and the Prothonotary's Office first.

Delaware also taxes the sale. Under 30 Del. C. section 5404, realty transfer tax has priority out of the proceeds of a judicial sale, except where the buyer files an affidavit that the transfer to a defaulted lender is exempt.

When does the Superior Court confirm a Delaware sheriff sale?

Under Superior Court Civil Rule 69(d), the sheriff's return is due on the third Monday of the month after the sale, objections must be filed by the first Thursday after the return date, and if there is no objection the sale is confirmed automatically the following Friday.

Sussex County describes the same rhythm for its sales, saying sales are confirmed on the first Friday after the third Monday of the following month. Kent County adds that the buyer's attorney prepares the deed after confirmation and the sheriff signs it.

After confirmation, 10 Del. C. section 4976 requires the sheriff to deliver a good and sufficient deed. Section 4985 says the real estate is discharged from liens against the defendant, except prior mortgages, to the extent the sale proceeds apply. A purchaser is entitled to rent from the day of sale under section 4978.

Ownership changes only when a proper deed is recorded, as Sussex County says on its sale page. See our guide to recording a Delaware deed for the fees and affidavits.

Can an owner get back money left over after a sheriff sale?

Possibly. If a sale brings in more than the debt, the court may hold the excess. Delaware's Superior Court runs a page called Project Rightful Owner that lists former owners, sold property addresses, court-held amounts, sale dates and case numbers for New Castle, Kent and Sussex counties.

The Delaware Code, in 10 Del. C. section 4986, says proceeds that cannot be paid because the entitled persons are absent, unknown or incompetent are paid into the court that issued the process. Payment into court discharges the selling officer from liability for that money.

The Project Rightful Owner pages point claimants to petition requirements and attorney listings. If you lost a house at a sheriff sale in the past, search the list by surname.

What can I do before my Delaware house goes to sheriff sale?

You can sell the house before the sale date, and a sale before the auction lets you keep any equity. Kent County's procedures show that tax sales have a redemption period of about 90 days, with the buyer receiving the bid back plus 15 percent if the owner redeems, while foreclosure sales have no redemption period.

In Sussex County, monition property cannot be possessed until 60 days after confirmation, and for sheriff sale property the county states that occupants are not automatically evicted. A buyer at auction should plan for that.

Steps worth taking:

  • Get the exact sale date and case number from the sheriff and the Prothonotary.
  • Ask the plaintiff's attorney for a payoff figure.
  • Consider whether a sale to a buyer who closes quickly beats the auction result.
  • Check for the loss-mitigation and mediation steps listed in the official summary above, which apply to owner-occupied homes.

A cash buyer can often close faster than an auction timeline allows, but the sale must still pay off the liens of record. Cash Home Buyers cannot promise a price and will review the numbers with you.

More questions about Delaware Sheriff Sales

What is a sheriff sale in Delaware?

It is a public auction of real estate conducted by the county sheriff under a court order, usually after a mortgage foreclosure or for unpaid taxes. The sale must be confirmed by the Superior Court before a deed is delivered.

Is there a redemption period after a Delaware foreclosure sale?

Kent County says foreclosure sales have no redemption period. Tax sales do: under the Delaware Code the owner has 60 days after the court approves the sale to redeem by paying the buyer the price plus 15 percent and costs.

How much do I need to bid at a Delaware sheriff sale?

Kent and Sussex counties both require a $4,000 deposit to bid. On a foreclosure the winner then pays 20 percent of the bid in total on sale day and the balance by the third Monday of the following month.

Do sheriff sale buyers get the keys right away?

No. Sussex County says occupants are not automatically evicted and that buyers may not enter before confirmation. Ownership changes when a proper deed is recorded.

Can a sheriff sale be stopped or postponed?

Sussex County says a sale can be stayed until 9:30 a.m. on sale day. Courts can also set aside a sale for irregularities, as in New Castle County v. Coleman in 2026, so owners and lenders should watch for notice of any change.

Can I sell my house instead of waiting for the auction?

Yes. You can sell before the sale date as long as the payoff of the liens of record is covered at closing. Contact the plaintiff's attorney for a payoff figure.

What the official sources say

  • Each county has a Recorder of Deeds; the recorder may require payment of recording fees once the date of reception is noted. (9 Del. C. § 9607(a); source)
  • Each recorded document carries a $5 Housing Development Fund surcharge and a $25 Delaware Cultural Access Fund fee, included in the county assessment fee. (9 Del. C. § 9607(b); source)
  • A recorder may accept electronic documents but must continue to accept paper documents; fees and taxes may be collected electronically. (25 Del. C. ch. 1, subch. V; source)
  • Before recording a deed from a nonresident individual or entity, the recorder collects the required tax return and estimated income tax. (9 Del. C. § 9607(e); source)

Where do I record a deed in Delaware?

You record a deed with the Recorder of Deeds in the county where the land sits, which means New Castle, Kent or Sussex County. Title 25 of the Delaware Code says a deed recorded in one county only has effect for land in that county.

The three offices are separate, and each sets its own fee schedule. State law says the fees of the New Castle and Sussex recorders are set by ordinance, and Kent's are set the same way.

  • New Castle County: 800 N. French St., 4th Floor, Wilmington, DE 19801. The recorder's office phone is (302) 395-7700.
  • Kent County: the Deeds Office at the county administrative complex, 555 Bay Rd., Dover. Kent lists (302) 744-2300 and weekday hours of 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
  • Sussex County: 2 The Circle, Georgetown, DE 19947. Hours are 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday to Friday, and the recording window closes at 4:00 p.m.

New Castle's recorder describes the office as the repository for all land transaction records, corporate filings and financing statements in the county. Sussex County says its office's mission is recording and indexing documents correctly and collecting the right fees and taxes.

What does the recorder require before accepting a Delaware deed?

The recorder will not accept a deed until it meets a short list of statutory requirements. The list below comes from 9 Del. C. section 9605 and 30 Del. C. chapter 54.

  • Affidavit of residence and gain: a deed conveying title to real estate must come with the affidavit unless the transfer is one of the exempt transactions in the transfer tax law.
  • Preparer's name: the deed must contain the words "prepared by" followed by the name and address of the person who drafted it.
  • Value: the deed must state the true, full and complete value, or come with an affidavit that gives the value and the reason, if any, that the deed is not taxable.
  • Proof of tax: no taxable document is recorded without proof that the realty transfer tax was paid.
  • Correct fees: Kent County says deeds cannot be recorded until the correct fees and taxes are collected, and a $20 rejection fee may apply.

Some deeds need extra language. If a lot in an unincorporated suburban community fronts a private road that the State does not maintain, the deed must say so before the recorder can record it.

Anyone who prepares a deed for a sale to a cash buyer should treat this list as a checklist. A missing preparer line or affidavit means a rejected deed and a closing that slips.

How much does it cost to record a deed in Delaware?

Recording fees are small next to the transfer tax, and they vary by county. Kent County publishes a schedule effective June 1, 2024, and New Castle County has announced an increase effective September 28, 2026.

ItemKent CountyNew Castle County
Document fee$36.00 (includes $30 State, $1 County, $5 Technology)A county fee schedule on its site lists a $30.00 state document fee per document
Page fee$10.00 per page, including the first pageRises from $13.00 to $15.00 per page on Sept. 28, 2026
Technology feeIncluded in document feeRises from $5.00 to $7.00 on Sept. 28, 2026
Deed extra$5.00 per tax parcel (map number)Check the current schedule
Non-conforming document$40.00Check the current schedule
Rejection$20.00Check the current schedule

Every recorded document also carries two statutory charges. Under 9 Del. C. section 9607, the recorder collects a $5 Housing Development Fund surcharge and a $25 Delaware Cultural Access Fund fee, and these are included in the county's assessment fee.

Sussex County's fee schedule was not available in the pages we reviewed, so call (302) 855-7785 before you send a check.

What is the Delaware realty transfer tax and who pays it?

The realty transfer tax is 3 percent of the property's value, or 2.5 percent where the county or municipality has enacted the full 1.5 percent local tax. The statute says it is split equally between grantor and grantee, and section 5412 puts the burden on the grantor unless the parties agree otherwise.

The Delaware Code counts "value" as the actual consideration, including liens and encumbrances. If the price is lower than the highest appraised value for local tax purposes, value means that appraised figure unless a party shows fair market value is lower. The code says proof of an arm's length sale between unrelated parties is enough to show fair market value.

A few rules matter to sellers in particular:

  • No tax applies if the value is under $100.
  • A first-time home buyer's share is reduced by one half of one percent of the lesser of the value or $400,000. The reduction applies to the grantee's portion only and does not lower the seller's.
  • Payment is shown by documentary stamp or another method the Department of Finance allows, and the recorder acts as the stamp agent.
  • On a judicial sale, the tax is paid first out of the proceeds, ahead of other claims and costs.

The code sets penalties for avoiding the tax. Presenting a document without the full tax paid is unlawful, with a fine up to $500 and up to one year in prison.

Municipal rates can add to the county's. Kent County's recorder publishes a rate form for state, county and municipal taxes, and its page directs tax questions to the Division of Revenue Tax Conferee at (302) 577-8651.

Which Delaware deeds are exempt from realty transfer tax?

Section 5401 of Title 30 lists more than two dozen kinds of conveyance that are not taxed as documents. Several come up often in home sales and family transfers.

  • Wills and transfer on death deeds, and mortgages.
  • Conveyances between spouses, and between former spouses after the divorce decree for property acquired during the marriage.
  • Conveyances between parent and child, between siblings, and between grandparent and grandchild.
  • A conveyance to a lender holding a bona fide mortgage that is genuinely in default, whether through a sheriff's foreclosure sale or a deed in lieu of foreclosure.
  • Conveyances to or from the United States, Delaware, their agencies and political subdivisions, and certain nonprofits.
  • Conveyances to a land bank.

Exempt does not mean unrecorded. The deed or an accompanying affidavit still has to give the value and the reason the document is exempt. For a foreclosure purchase by the lender, the grantee makes the affidavit.

If you inherit a Delaware house and want to deed it to a sibling, the sibling exemption can apply. A tax professional or attorney should confirm the exemption before closing.

Can I record a Delaware deed electronically?

Yes, if the county recorder has chosen to accept electronic documents. The electronic recording subchapter of Title 25 lets a recorder receive, index and store electronic documents under standards set by the Electronic Recording Commission, which includes each county's recorder and two members appointed by the Secretary of State.

A recorder that accepts electronic documents must keep accepting paper ones and must index both in the same index. Fees and taxes may be collected electronically. An electronic signature satisfies a signature requirement, and notarization can be met when the notary's electronic signature and other required information are attached to the document.

Sussex County's recorder runs a recording activity notification service, and its deed records are searchable online, and Kent County links an online deed search from its Deeds Office page. Each office decides what it will accept, so ask before you plan on e-recording.

Does a nonresident seller owe tax at recording?

A nonresident seller may have estimated income tax collected at the recorder's counter. Under 9 Del. C. section 9607(e), before the recorder records a deed from a nonresident individual, pass-through entity or corporation, the recorder collects the required tax return and the estimated income tax reported due, if any.

The recorder remits that money to the Secretary of Finance by the 20th of the month after recording. This applies to the seller's state income tax on a gain, and it is separate from the transfer tax.

Owners who live outside Delaware, which is common for inherited and rental property, should ask the closing agent about this return early. A missing return holds up the deed.

More questions about Delaware Recording a Deed

How long does it take to record a deed in Delaware?

The pages reviewed do not state a standard turnaround. Sussex County closes its recording window at 4:00 p.m. each business day, and the recorder notes the date of reception once the instrument is received. Ask the office or your title company for current timing.

What is the Delaware realty transfer tax rate?

The state statute sets 3 percent of value, or 2.5 percent where the county or municipality has enacted the full 1.5 percent local tax. The tax is shared equally by buyer and seller unless the contract says otherwise.

Who pays the transfer tax in Delaware, the buyer or the seller?

The statute apportions it equally between grantor and grantee. As between the parties, the grantor bears the burden unless they agree differently, so the sales contract controls.

Is there a first-time home buyer break on Delaware transfer tax?

Yes. The buyer's share is reduced by one half of one percent of the lesser of the value or $400,000. The break applies to the buyer's portion only.

What does the recorder need on the deed?

A deed needs a stated value or value affidavit, proof of transfer tax payment unless exempt, an affidavit of residence and gain, and the words "prepared by" with the preparer's name and address.

Can I record a deed without paying the fees up front?

No. The recorder may require payment once the date of reception is noted, and Kent County says deeds cannot be recorded until the correct fees and taxes are collected.
